label: churn200-s3
summary: This churn network predicts churn through three chained routes, gathered in serviceIntlUsageCore: many customer-service calls (serviceCallsLowDay, which turns on sooner when day usage is low, relayed by state11ServiceGate, which is held off in Hawaii), the international plan (intlPlanGate) and heavy day usage (heavyUsageNoVmail, whose threshold rises with voicemail messages). The routes damp each other: once the service-call relay is on, the international-plan unit shrinks, and the plan in turn lowers the heavy-usage unit. The 1778 training customers with at least one route unit on churn at 28.9%, the other 2222 at 2.3%; switching the core off lowers the training AUC from 0.918 to 0.629. A linear part (directTerms) adds a strong voicemail-plan reduction (-0.99 per sd) and state terms; stateBumps adds a few per-state offsets, the largest being an Arkansas reduction fitted to 78 training customers whose churn rate is not lower than the rest; vmailNightUnits and state17Gate are small. The annotated model reproduces the network to within 4.4e-16, with structural and compositional coverage complete. The predicted risks run high (mean 37% against a churn rate of 14.1%), so they rank customers rather than give calibrated probabilities.

(2) Not a bug but a trap: after add_identity_node on the output, query_ablate(direct=true) reports 0 direct edges of the root; edge weights were read with query_ablate(edges=['<input>->identity_0', ...]). (3) Annotate refuses a hidden node that is the exit of one leaf as an entry of another ('already covered'); chaining leaves needed add_identity_node on each leaf-to-leaf edge (identity_1044, identity_4939, identity_5868, identity_7494).
